subject: Request: SLA offset calculation & approval for May 15 incident
messages:

Subject: SLA impact on May 15 — request for offset calculations

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the postmortem posted earlier this week. Our finance team has asked us to submit a formal request for the SLA offsets/credits related to the May 15 incident (service degraded between ~02:42–03:27 PDT). They're asking for:

- an eligibility confirmation under our 99.95% availability commitment,
- a clear minutes-of-downtime calculation by region/time window, and
- the dollar credit equivalent (or % of monthly invoice) plus how it will be applied (invoice adjustment or standalone credit).

We also need the related logs and any event IDs to reconcile with our internal monitoring. I've attached a short spreadsheet with our observed impact windows for the affected services. Can you confirm next steps and an ETA for a formal calculation?

Appreciate it — we're hoping to close this on our May month-end.

Best,

Hi Elena — thanks for the note and for the spreadsheet. We're sorry for the disruption on May 15. I've looped in Laura from Customer Success to ensure the customer reconciliation is smooth.

Prelim notes: based on the incident timeline in the postmortem and our internal telemetry, the affected region (us-west-2) saw ~45 minutes of sustained degraded request success for the multi-tenant hosted inference route. Roughly speaking, that would put you into the SLA credit band for a single-month availability breach.

Next steps (ETA in my calendar):
- I will work with Billing (Rishi) to run the formal minutes-to-credit calculation and convert to the appropriate invoice offset. ETA: 48 hours.
- We'll attach the internal event IDs and filtered logs you requested.

I'll send a follow-up with the exact credit amount and the proposed issuance method (invoice adjustment vs. credit issuance). If you have an internal invoice number to tie this to, send it over and we'll reference it.

Thanks again for the patience — will be back shortly with numbers.

Team — forwarding LumenBridge's request. Key asks: eligibility confirmation, minutes calculation, dollar equivalent, and attachment of logs.

Notes for context (internal):
- Customer: LumenBridge (multi-tenant hosted API, billed monthly).
- Incident: May 15, 02:42–03:27 PDT, degraded request success on hosted inference route.
- SLA: 99.95% monthly availability (per contract).

What I need from Billing: 1) standard minutes->credit table we use, 2) recommended issuance mechanic (invoice adjustment vs. credit voucher), and 3) whether this requires executive approval for credits > $25k. Please run the calculation against customer usage for May (I'll attach traffic slice).

I'll include the telemetry slice in a separate email.

— Vivek

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 14:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SLA impact on May 15 — request for offset calculations

Vivek / Laura — ran the numbers against LumenBridge's May usage. Summary below (attached full calc workbook):

Calculation approach:
- We use the contract's SLA table: availability >= 99.95% = no credit; 99.90–99.95 = 5% monthly credit; 99.0–99.90 = 10% credit; <99.0 = 25% credit.
- For May, their billed ECUs (inference compute units) were 1,120, total monthly invoice (hosting + usage) = $98,400.
- Using region-specific telemetry, impacted window is 45 minutes of degraded success. We translate that to availability as: (total minutes in month - unavailable minutes)/total minutes. May total minutes = 44,640 (31 days). Unavailable minutes = 45 -> availability = 99.8999% (rounded 99.90%).

Result: availability falls into the 99.90–99.95 band => eligible for 5% monthly credit.

Credit math (two presentation options):
A) Percentage on invoice: 5% of $98,400 = $4,920. Applied as invoice adjustment on next invoice (June).
B) Fixed-dollar credit voucher: we can issue a $4,920 credit token tied to their account, usable over 12 months.

Policy check: credits > $25k need Director sign-off. This one is below that threshold. No exec sign-off required per finance policy.

Attachments: lumenbridge_sla_calcs_20260520.xlsx (detailed calc workbook) — includes the minute-by-minute availability slice and event IDs. Also attached incident logs zip for customer reconciliation.

Recommendation: Issue 5% invoice adjustment (Option A) unless the customer prefers a voucher. I'll draft the adjustment line for the June invoice; Vivek / Laura confirm and proceed.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Billing Operations | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Attachments: lumenbridge_sla_calcs_20260520.xlsx, incident-20260515-logs.zip

Hi Elena — following up with the formal calculation and next steps. Thank you for the spreadsheet you shared; it matched our telemetry.

Summary of outcome (final):
- Eligibility: Yes — LumenBridge's May availability measured at ~99.90% for the affected hosted route, which falls within the 99.90–99.95 band.
- Credit: 5% of the May invoice = $4,920. Options for issuance:
  1) Invoice adjustment: We will apply a -$4,920 line item to your June invoice (our recommended default).
  2) Account credit voucher: a $4,920 voucher valid for 12 months.

What we will do next:
- By default we will apply option (1) unless you tell us otherwise before May 29.
- Attached are: (a) the detailed calculation workbook, (b) filtered event IDs and logs needed for your reconciliation.
- We have (per internal finance) no special approvals required — credit is below Director threshold.

If you prefer a voucher instead of an invoice adjustment, reply and we'll issue a voucher token and send redemption instructions.

Again, apologies for the impact. If you want a brief call to walk through the calc workbook, Laura and I are available next week.

Best,
— Vivek
